title: Refactor button density variants, token scoping, and publish gating
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
We need to simplify the button component family by reducing density-related variant duplication, introduce token-scoped sizing variables (button.content-*), clean auto-layout constraints across instances, and add a non-destructive publish gating workflow. The goal is predictable spacing across density scales, smaller token surface area, and fewer brittle instances that break when token names change.

Background:
Over the past year we accumulated button variants for compact/regular/comfortable across multiple button styles (primary, secondary, ghost). Each style contains repeated named tokens (padding-small, padding-medium, padding-large) and duplicated auto-layout constraints. This causes frequent breakages when token names are migrated and increases cognitive load for engineers consuming the design token export. Engineering has reported mapping inconsistencies in the token JSON and runtime CSS.

Goals:
1) Consolidate density variants down to a single density axis with token-scoped sizing (example tokens: button.content-height, button.content-horizontal-gap, button.icon-gap).
2) Migrate existing instances without breaking layouts in 95% of cases; provide migration notes for the remaining 5%.
3) Remove nested auto-layout constraints and standardize frame anchors so instances respect parent resizing and container stacks.
4) Add a publish gating checklist in Figma library to prevent accidental publishing of token name changes.
5) Ensure a11y contrast and touch target compliance for all density scales.

Out of scope:
- Re-skinning of button visuals unrelated to spacing (color/typography updates will be separate).
- Runtime CSS changes (handled by ENG once tokens are finalized).

Approach:
1) Audit: run instance finder to collect all button instances across files (team files + product files) and categorize by usage patterns.
2) Token scoping: create a token namespace for button internals (button.content-*) and map existing tokens to the new ones with a deprecation table.
3) Variants: replace multiple manual variant sets with a single density variant (compact | regular | comfortable) exposed via a single variant property. Reduce state variants per style to: default, hover, focused, disabled.
4) Auto-layout: normalize button frame to single auto-layout direction with explicit horizontal padding via token references; remove nested frames used only for spacing.
5) Publish gating: add a library publishing checklist (linked doc + required reviewer) and a short script that validates token name changes against the deprecation table before allowing publish.

Deliverables:
- Figma library: updated button component with new token references and simplified variant set.
- Migration guide: Confluence doc with example mappings, known edge cases, and a codemod snippet engineers can use to update token keys in their manifests.
- Publish checklist: checklist + mandatory approver list inside Figma library team.

Acceptance criteria:
- New button components render with expected spacing in 95% of sampled instances across product files.
- Token export shows button.content-* keys without duplicated synonyms.
- Autosave publish attempt blocked by checklist if token keys are changed without reviewer sign-off.
- Design review sign-off from PM (Liam O'Connor) and Eng tech lead (Priya Shah).

Migration notes (high level):
- We will keep legacy tokens for 3 months (deprecation aliases) and create a codemod for token key replacement in the token JSON used by infra.
- For complex instances where layout breaks (rare), we'll add manual migration tickets and label them DES-MIGRATE-XXXX.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Liam O'Connor
- Eng: Priya Shah (tech lead), frontend: Marco Rivera
- Design Ops: Noor Patel

QA checks:
- Manual spot checks across 12 high-traffic product screens.
- Token export validation: run token-diff against previous export and ensure mapping table exists for any renamed keys.
- Accessibility sweep for touch target and contrast on all density sizes.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Broad use of custom instances that rely on legacy layer names -> Mitigation: codemod + migration backlog + communication to teams with example fixes.
- Risk: Publish gating may slow down designers -> Mitigation: add fast-track approval and a 24-hour SLAs for reviewer responses.

Rollout plan:
Week 1: Audit and prototype (this ticket)
Week 2: Implement token scope & variant restructure in a draft library file; start codemod work (ENG)
Week 3: Migration run on sample product files; fix edge cases; prepare publish checklist
Week 4: Finalize and publish behind an opt-in flag; communicate to internal teams; start deprecation clock

Links/Artifacts:
- Figma draft file: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/button-density-refactor
- Token mapping doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DS/Button+Token+Mapping
- Codemod PR (internal GH): https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-tokens/pull/214

Notes for reviewers:
- Please pay close attention to instances that include icons and mixed vertical centering; those were the most brittle in the audit.
- Verify token export names match engineering's expected JSON shape in the PR linked above.
